headline_marked: [[AI Copilot Autofix]] Introduced Critical Snowflake Jira Vulnerability
headline: AI Copilot Autofix Introduced Critical Snowflake Jira Vulnerability
summary: An AI coding assistant's commit inadvertently created a script injection flaw, allowing access to Jira credentials before being patched.
details: Wiz Research's AI tool, Red Agent, discovered a critical vulnerability in a public Snowflake repository. The flaw allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary commands within a GitHub Actions runner by opening a specially crafted GitHub issue.

The vulnerability was introduced on June 18, 2026, by a commit co-authored by GitHub Copilot's Autofix feature. The AI assistant replaced a sanitized input pattern with direct string interpolation, creating the injection vector.
The issue was exploitable via the 'jira_issue.yml' workflow, which triggered on any new issue. An attacker could craft an issue title to break out of a shell script and exfiltrate Jira credentials.
Wiz successfully exfiltrated base64-encoded credentials from a GitHub Actions runner, granting read access to Snowflake's engineering, security compliance, and bug tracking projects.

Snowflake remediated the vulnerability the same day it was responsibly disclosed on June 23, 2026. They rotated the affected credential and confirmed via audit logs that Wiz was the sole actor during the exposure window.

This incident underscores the need for rigorous oversight of AI coding tools. AI-generated code must undergo the same security scrutiny as human-written code, as AI can inadvertently reintroduce insecure patterns.
caption:
AI coding assistants can introduce critical security flaws. A GitHub Copilot Autofix commit created a vulnerability in Snowflake's Jira.

Wiz Research's AI tool, Red Agent, discovered a critical vulnerability in a public Snowflake repository. The flaw allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary commands within a GitHub Actions runner by opening a specially crafted GitHub issue.

The vulnerability was introduced on June 18, 2026, by a commit co-authored by GitHub Copilot's Autofix feature. The AI assistant replaced a sanitized input pattern with direct string interpolation, creating the injection vector.

The issue was exploitable via the 'jira_issue.yml' workflow, which triggered on any new issue. An attacker could craft an issue title to break out of a shell script and exfiltrate Jira credentials.

Wiz successfully exfiltrated base64-encoded credentials from a GitHub Actions runner, granting read access to Snowflake's engineering, security compliance, and bug tracking projects.

Snowflake remediated the vulnerability the same day it was responsibly disclosed on June 23, 2026. They rotated the affected credential and confirmed via audit logs that Wiz was the sole actor during the exposure window.

This incident underscores the need for rigorous oversight of AI coding tools. AI-generated code must undergo the same security scrutiny as human-written code, as AI can inadvertently reintroduce insecure patterns.
